The '''Washington County Jail''' is a historic former civic building at 90 South College Avenue in [[Fayetteville, Arkansas]].  Built in 1896, this building was the fourth to serve as county jail and was in use until 1973, making it the longest tenured in county history.<ref>{{ cite web | title=Brief History of County Buildings |publisher=Washington County, Arkansas |url=http://www.co.washington.ar.us/index.aspx?page=500 |accessdate=2011-08-16 }}</ref>  The Romanesque Revival building was designed by W. B. Reese and is locally unusual and distinctive for its medieval appearance.  It is built out of load-bearing stone, square-cut and laid in irregular courses, with a rough quarry-cut finish.  Most of the building is of darker shades with trim in lighter shades. Nominally two stories in height, the rightmost bay has a square tower with a crenellated parapet.<ref name=NRHP>{{cite web|url=https://www.arkansasheritage.com/docs/default-source/national-registry/WA0393-pdf|title=NRHP nomination for Washington County Jail|publisher=Arkansas Preservation|accessdate=2015-04-06}}</ref>

The building, which is now in private hands, was listed on the [[National Register of Historic Places]] in 1978.<ref name="nris"/>
